messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#477] Re: Is there a dependence between RevolutionR and RHadoop?
parts:
For rmr:https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/rmr,  section #2
For rhdfs:https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/rhdfs, section #2
For rhbase:https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/rhbase, section #2

It seems from your reply that some details may be missing from those documents that you find necessary or at least helpful. Please let us know and we will try to improve them -- just found some outdated dependencies for instance. Let me be very clear that there is no single step that is specific to Revo R. There is some FUD circulating out there so we can't afford even an ambiguous statement.  Like other R packages (Rcurl is an example), the three RHadoop packages depend on external software independent of R (or Revolution for that matter), namely hadoop and thrift. Some shell variables allow R to find these external software. They also depend on some other R packages, as specified in the installation documents above and the DESCRIPTION file in each package. All the dependencies are open source. The RHadoop packages are loaded by the usual R function library. 

Antonio

The repo is for developers, not general users. The download page is here https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/Downloads

The downloads can be installed as they are. The install procedure knows which directories to use for what. Don't let me discourage you for developing an interest in the structure of R packages though. The reference document is http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html

The main page of the wiki is the place to start. https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki
As for Revo, Can you clarify what are the required/recommended options for the Revo R installation?

Unfortunately I am not the right person and this is not the best channel to get answers on that. I would suggest contacting Revo's support.  For Academic license I gather from their web site: "This offer only covers the Revolution R Enterprise software itself. Academic Users may receive free support from the Revolution Discussion Forums and inside-R.org Community Web site. Premium Technical Support options are available for an extra fee."
In particular, is RevoScaleR a required option or simply an automatic part of Revo R?
RevoScaleR is not required to use RHadoop, other than that I am not sure.

The installation I am talking about is of Revo Enterprise edition, academic license. I am installing it on a 16 node cluster in the San Diego Super Computer Center.  If you could point me to somebody else that has done this 

installation successfully in UCSD/SDSC that would be a great help.

Again please contact Revo through their support channels.



Antonio
